Exp8 — 10 roster MM2026-09-04

Descriptive, not causal. MMs appear by volume rank only.

Part of the Exp8 record · One-sided taker surges · set 3, 922 events

Exp8 one-sided taker surges, full record: what a side rule sees that the net rule does not

A second event definition. Each side of the taker flow gets its own score, and an event is a half hour in which one side surges (zB ≥ 3.81 for buys, zS ≥ 3.89 for sells) and dominates. That gives 922 side surges (family F1), tuned to match the 915 net-flow events in count. The section compares the two rules, times each surge on a 1-minute run, and reruns the section 4 population statistics on F1.

Key results

Roster shocks cluster where the two rules agree§9.3 →The added events are two-way half hours, not quiet ones§9.3 →A taker surge with a large price move against it is 11 events out of 1,730§9.5 →Every event set shocks four to seven times as many MMs as the same clock time on a quiet day§9.7 →

Section, table and figure numbers are those of the single Exp8 record, so they do not start at 1 here. Definitions shared by every section are in the notation and event-set sections of the main page.

Each finding shows its headline. Click one to read the explanation.

9. Side-surge event families

Event set 3, the 922 one-sided taker surges on 1-minute windows; the net-flow boxes (event set 1) appear only as a comparison column. F2 is the 399 half hours in which both sides surge and F3 the 327 one-sided events set 1 never selects. Selection is on 30-minute boxes; the event window [t0, t1) is the 1-minute run inside the box, and tc is the run minute of largest cumulative net flow. Overlap with the 181 roster shocks is counted in §9.3.
Symbols used on this page (one-sided surges)

Symbols used on this page (one-sided surges)

  • Side surge (F1): a 30-minute bin in which one side's own taker flow score reaches 3.81 (buys) or 3.89 (sells), built like the net-flow score on the prior 7 days, and that side carries at least half of the taker USD.
  • One-sided, two-sided: an event is one-sided when the surging side is flagged, its taker USD is at least the other side's in the bin and at least twice the other side's in the previous bin; it is two-sided when a side surged and no side meets that test.
  • F1, F2, F3: F1 is the 922 one-sided events, the sets BOTH and NEW_ONLY together. F2 is the 399 two-sided half hours: some side surges, no side passes the one-sided test, and |buys − sells| / (buys + sells) is below 1/3 in the peak bin. F3 is the 327 F1 events whose 30-minute box overlaps no net-flow event, the set NEW_ONLY.
  • Net-flow events (event set 1): the 915 events of section 3: runs of 30-minute bins in which HYPE net taker USD, buys minus sells, scores at least 3.70 in absolute value against the prior 7 days of bins (|zNET|, the top 5% of bins). On this page they are the comparison catalogue, measured on their 30-minute boxes.
  • 1-minute run, t0, t1: the event window [t0, t1) of a one-sided surge. Inside the event's 5-minute duration run, a minute belongs to the run when the surging side's taker USD less the other side's stays above a quarter of its 95th percentile over the prior 6 hours, with gaps of up to 3 minutes bridged, and the run holds at least one minute at 3 times that percentile. t0 is the open of the run's first minute and t1 the close of its last minute, an exclusive end, so the run lasts t1 − t0 minutes. UTC clock times, the same for every MM in the event.
  • tpv, flow peak: the run minute with the most surge-side taker USD.
  • tc, pressure peak: the run minute at which the cumulative in-direction net taker USD, summed from t0, is largest.
  • tpp, price extreme: the minute of the largest mid move in the surge direction from p0, searched over [t0, t1 + 15 min).
  • p0: the mid at t0, read at the first tick of the run's first minute.
  • sig24: the MM's own position scale, in HYPE, recomputed for each event from its positions over the 24 hours before t0. It is the largest of three numbers: 1.4826 times the median absolute deviation of the position from its trailing 6-hour median, 2% of its 95th-percentile absolute position, and $12,500 of HYPE at the t0 mid.
  • Shocked: the MM's HYPE position changed from t0 to t1 by at least 3 sig24 (at least $37,500). It is decided per MM per event: the same MM can be shocked in one event and unshocked in the next.
  • Absorption side, exit side: the absorption side is the maker side the event's takers trade against (the bid when takers sell, the ask when takers buy); an MM filled there builds a position against the flow. The exit (opposite) side is the other one.
  • Roster: the ten named HYPE MMs, MM01 to MM10, of the earlier per-wallet shock study.
  • Recall, lift: recall is the share of the 181 roster shocks that fall inside a rule's events; lift is how many times more often a flagged bin holds a roster shock than a random bin.
  • Markout M30, M60, M120: what a fill is worth against the mid 30, 60 or 120 minutes later, in bps of the fill's USD; positive is favourable to the wallet.

Selecting on a surge in one taker side, at the same number of events as the net-flow rule of §3, keeps 595 of that rule's boxes and adds 327 new ones. The added events are half hours where both sides ran hot and the net stayed small, and they almost never contain a roster MM inventory shock: 8 of the 181, against 87 for the overlapping half. The MM outcome pass covers all three families: against matched quiet windows, F1, F3 and F2 each shock four to seven times as many MMs (§9.7).

Population and grain
  • Population. 1,730 target events over 2025-03-27 to 2026-06-30: 595 BOTH, 327 NEW_ONLY, 330 ZNET_ONLY, 478 TWO_SIDED. Every exhibit includes 2025-10-10 and 2026-01-31.
  • Grain. One row is one event. Quantiles are p5 / p25 / p50 / p75 / p95 over events.

9.1 How F1 is built

  • Active MM: a labelled HYPE MM with at least one post-only (ALO) fill in the 2 hours before the event and at least one fill inside it.
  • Event classes: liquidation cascade: forced flow at least 10% of taker USD; otherwise big price move: the mid moved at least 168 bps from start to end, the top 5% of all half hours; otherwise no big price move.
Terms used here: HYPE MM, Active MM, PRE2H, PRE30, POST, ALO, IOC, GTC, Forced, voluntary flow, Quantile cells, 2025-10-10, v5d, Event classes
  • HYPE MM: a wallet the project's daily label model (v5d) classes as a HYPE market maker on that date. The label is per date.
  • Active MM: a labelled HYPE MM with at least one post-only (ALO) fill in the 2 hours before the event and at least one fill inside it. On a date whose whole population has no post-only fill in those 2 hours, a maker fill counts instead: 2026-04-16 to 2026-04-23, when the fill table has no time-in-force.
  • PRE2H, PRE30, POST: PRE2H is the 2 hours ending at t0; PRE30 the last 30 minutes before t0; POST the 2 hours after t1.
  • ALO, IOC, GTC: order types: ALO is post-only (rejected if it would cross), IOC is immediate-or-cancel, GTC rests until cancelled.
  • Forced, voluntary flow: forced flow is taker USD from liquidations and auto-deleveraging (ADL); voluntary flow is all other taker USD. A victim is the wallet that was force-closed.
  • Quantile cells: a cell with five numbers is p5 / p25 / p50 / p75 / p95; with three, p25 / p50 / p75.
  • 2025-10-10: the liquidation-cascade day, kept in the row-level tables and named wherever it moves a result. On its 21:00 event 86.8% of absorbing-side maker USD ($517m of $596m) went to wallets with no MM label, against a median of 33.4% on other events, and 10 of 41 shocked MMs were shocked in the opposite direction.
  • v5d: the project's daily wallet label: a fixed set of threshold rules, not a fitted model, that reads each wallet's order records for one coin on one day and labels it market maker, frontend or algorithmic taker, in that order of test. It covers 2025-03-27 to 2026-06-30 and labels a wallet separately on each coin and date.
  • Event classes: liquidation cascade: forced flow at least 10% of taker USD; otherwise big price move: the mid moved at least 168 bps from start to end, the top 5% of all half hours; otherwise no big price move.
Construction steps

F1: one-sided side-surge events, as built by code/redef4_events.py (stage sel30) and code/redef4_steps.py (stages targets, dur5, anchor, catalog)

  • Taker flow per bin. Bt and St are HYPE taker buy and taker sell USD in 30-minute bin t (data/redef_imb_measures_30m.parquet). For side a, Vat is that side’s USD and Vot the other side’s.
  • Side score. zat=(Vat−mat)/max(1.4826 MADat, 25000), where mat and MADat are the median and median absolute deviation of Va over the 336 bins (7 days) strictly before t, with at least 40% of them observed. The $25,000 floor binds in 0 of 21,923 valid bins per side.
  • Surge flag. A side is flagged in a bin when zat≥ca. The cutoffs are the full-sample 94.25% quantile of each side’s score, cB=3.81 and cS=3.89. The quantile 0.9425 is the one that gives as many one-sided events (922) as the net-flow catalogue has (915).
  • One-sided bin. Side a is one-sided in bin t when it is flagged, Vat≥Vot and Vat≥2 Vot−1: the surging side carries at least half of the bin’s taker USD and at least twice what the other side traded in the previous bin. A bin with a surge on some side and no one-sided side is two-sided.
  • 30-minute box. Flagged bins of the same class (one-sided buy, one-sided sell) are merged into a run, with one unflagged bin allowed between two flagged ones. The box is the run’s span; its peak bin is the bin with the largest surging-side score. F1 is every one-sided box: 922 events, 439 buy and 483 sell, on 349 dates, 3 of them on 2025-10-10.
  • Duration run D, 5 minutes. Around each flagged half hour, plus one 30-minute bin on each side, the build looks for 5-minute bins in which the surging side’s volume is unusually high for that side: its 5-minute score is at or above the full-sample 90th percentile, 3.33 for buys and 3.51 for sells, and the surging side traded at least as much as the other side in the bin. D is the run of such bins that holds the largest surge-side bin of the search window, with one bin that fails the test allowed inside the run; where no run holds that bin, D is the run with the most surge-side USD.
  • 1-minute window: where the surge starts and ends. Inside D plus 5 minutes on each side, a minute belongs to a run when its in-direction net taker USD, the surging side’s USD less the other side’s, stays above the stay threshold (0.25× p95), where p95 is the 95th percentile of that measure over the 360 minutes before the search window, floored at $5,000; gaps of up to 3 minutes are bridged. A run counts when at least one of its minutes reaches the enter threshold (3× p95); 63 events qualify only at 2× p95. The strongest run, the one with the largest total net USD, is the event window [t0, t1): t0 is the open of its first minute and t1 the close of its last. In 32 events no run reaches either threshold, and [t0, t1) is D itself.
  • Event window used by the population build. The run [t0, t1) itself; its length t1−t0 is a median 14 minutes, p5 4, p25 9, p75 23, p95 38. peak_utc is tc. The event side (hit_side) is the surging side a; the absorption side is the maker side opposite it.
  • Sets inside F1. BOTH (595): the box overlaps one of the 915 net-flow 30-minute boxes. NEW_ONLY (327): it overlaps none.
  • Classes. The event class in the population tables follows the absolute price rule, as for the net-flow catalogue: liquidation cascade when forced taker USD is at least 10% of the box, otherwise big move when the box start-to-end mid move is at least 168.36 bps; F1 has 47 cascade, 314 big-move and 561 other events.

For contrast: the net-flow catalogue, F2 and F3

  • Net-flow catalogue (§3, 915 events). The same 7-day robust score computed on net taker USD Bt−St in 30-minute bins, flagged when |zNET|≥3.70, the full-sample 95% quantile. Its population windows are the 30-minute boxes (median 30 minutes, up to 180).
  • F2, two-sided (399 events). Boxes of two-sided bins at the same cutoffs (some side surged, no side passed the one-sided test), kept when |I|<1/3 at the peak bin, I=(B−S)/(B+S); 79 of 478 are dropped by that test. The 5-minute run uses a score on total taker USD B+S (cutoff 3.06) with no side condition. The 1-minute run uses the excess Xt=(Bt+St)−median6h(B+S) in place of Nt, with the same 3, 2 and 0.25 multiples of its 6-hour p95, and the direction is the sign of the run’s cumulative net flow. On all 478 two-sided candidates these runs are long: median 30 minutes, p95 96.
  • F3, side-only (327 events). The NEW_ONLY part of F1: one-sided boxes that overlap no net-flow event. Same windows as in F1.

9.2 Definitions

The four sets
  • The four sets. BOTH (595) are one-sided boxes that overlap an event of the §3 catalogue. NEW_ONLY (327) are one-sided boxes that overlap none. ZNET_ONLY (330) are §3 events no side-surge box touches. TWO_SIDED (478) are the two-sided boxes at the same cutoffs.

  • Roster shocks cluster where the two rules agree.
    87 of the 181 shocks sit inside a BOTH box against 8 inside a NEW_ONLY box, and per bin flagged BOTH is 8.1 times random against 1.6 for NEW_ONLY. When the other side also traded heavily, roster MMs rarely ended with a large position.
  • The added events are two-way half hours, not quiet ones.
    NEW_ONLY carries $22.0m of taker USD, close to BOTH's $28.6m, but its median |imbalance| is 0.15 against 0.35 and its median box move is 91 bps against 156. Both sides ran hot in 88.7% of them.
  • Many events that only the net-flow rule selects have no dominant side.
    Of the ZNET_ONLY events, 47.3% have a side surge at the side-surge cutoffs and 38.2% have a bin that passes the one-sided test. ZNET_ONLY is the smallest set by taker USD.
  • TWO_SIDED events are the largest and the longest.
    Median $30.1m of taker USD, p95 $135.8m, and 36.0% run past one 30-minute bin.
  • The added half hours clear the surging side’s own volume threshold and stay under the net rule. Their median surge-side score is 5.0 against 6.9 in BOTH, while their median |zNET| is 2.4 against 5.7, below the 3.70 the net-flow rule needs. The opposite side trades about as much as it does in a BOTH event, a median $8.7m against $8.9m, while the surge side is smaller, $13.1m against $19.3m, so the median net imbalance is 0.15 against 0.35. Source tables/f1r0922_newonly_vs_both.csv.

  • The run opens a median 8 minutes into the labelled half hour and closes a median 24 minutes in.
    22% of one-sided runs open before the label and 21% close after the labelled box ends, so the box boundary cuts the run in roughly one event in five.
  • Pressure keeps building after the flow peak.
    tc sits a median 4 minutes after tpv, p95 21 minutes, and by tpv a median 79% of the run’s cumulative net flow is already in. In 76% of one-sided events tc is the last minute of the run.
  • 74% of runs end because the other side takes over
    , 20% because flow dries up, and 6% because the search window ran out. 3.5% of one-sided events have no qualifying 1-minute run and use the 5-minute duration run.
  • Two-sided events are long.
    Their runs are a median 30 minutes long and start a median 14 minutes before the bin label. They sit a median 19 minutes before the roster wallet begins to form its position, against 2 minutes for one-sided events.

9.5 Price path after the surge

Fifteen minutes after the run the median big move still holds two thirds of its peak. Over the next two hours, how far the price comes back follows the taker flow after the run, not the inventory the market makers took on or how they quote.

Terms used here: peak move, final move, share kept, big-move threshold g, price patterns
  • Peak move: the largest mid move in the surge direction from p0 over [t0, t1+15 min), in basis points (bps). It is reached at tpp.
  • Final move: the mid at t1+15 min against p0, in bps, signed in the surge direction.
  • Share kept: the final move divided by the peak move, read only on events whose peak move reaches g.
  • Big-move threshold g: the full-sample 95th percentile of the peak move for the event’s run-length class: 153 bps for runs of up to 15 minutes, 195 bps for 16 to 30, 240 bps for 31 to 60 and 320 bps for longer runs. Every event of one length class is judged against the same threshold.
  • Price patterns: small price move: the peak move stays below g and the final move above −g. Against: the peak move stays below g and the final move is g or more against the surge. Held: the share kept is at least 0.75. Partly reverted: from 0.25 to 0.75. Reverted: below 0.25.

  • A taker surge with a large price move against it is 11 events out of 1,730.
    Direction is close to guaranteed once the move is big enough to clear the threshold.
  • Reversion is four times as common in the side-surge families as in the net-flow-only set
    , 6.7% to 7.7% against 1.5%. Among one-sided events whose move cleared the threshold, the median keeps 68% of its peak move at t1+15 min, with a quarter keeping under 47% and a quarter over 85%.
  • The price extreme does not reliably follow the pressure peak.
    The median gap from tc to tpp is 0 minutes, and tpp is within 2 minutes of tc in 49.5% of one-sided events.
  • Which F1 events count as big moves depends on the threshold.
    The run-length class threshold passes 53.4% of F1 events, the same threshold computed within the event's own date passes 59.3%, and the 168 bps start-to-end threshold on the 30-minute box passes 37.1%. The class threshold and the 168 bps threshold agree on 70.5% of events; 211 F1 events peak above their class threshold and give part of it back before the box ends.

Two hours after the run, in five buckets

Cut into fifths by the return 120 minutes after the run, the deepest-reversal fifth gives back 1.31 times its own peak move at the median, and the continuation fifth moves a further 155 bps the surge way. The two fifths put the same inventory on the MM population; what differs afterwards is the taker flow and the unwind, not the quoting.

Terms used here: reversal return, buckets, event clock, post-run imbalance, population and absorbers, population shock, lean at placement, cancels and book pressure, tests
  • Reversal return R(h): R(h)=−d·104·(mid(t1+h)/mid(t1)−1) in bps, for h of 5, 10, 30, 60 and 120 minutes after the run end, where mid(t) is the last mid of the 1-minute bin ending at t and d is +1 on a buy surge and −1 on a sell surge. Positive means the price came back toward p0. G(h)=R(h)/Mpeak is the share of the peak move given back.
  • Buckets Q1 to Q5: quintiles of R(120) over all 922 one-sided surges; Q1 is the continuation fifth, Q5 the deepest-reversal fifth. The edges are −84, 6, 78 and 191 bps, which is −0.32, 0.02, 0.27 and 0.66 dollars per HYPE. Quintiles taken on the gated events alone, and a fixed cut at −100, 0, 100 and 250 bps, order every result the same way. The 2026-05-19 00:00 buy surge, whose price extreme is a spike tick at $249.88, keeps its R(120) and is left out of every peak-move cell.
  • Event clock: 5-minute bins relative to t1, from −60 to +120 minutes; the median run of 14 minutes is the grey band in the figures. A bucket’s line is the median across its events of the event’s value in the bin.
  • Post-run imbalance: taker USD d·(buy−sell) summed over the 15 minutes after t1, positive when the flow keeps pushing the surge way; also as a share of the run’s surge-side taker USD.
  • Population and absorbers: the active MMs of the population of record, 97,869 (event, MM) rows, a median of 100 per event. Floors of at least 50 and at least 100 HYPE limit orders inside [t0, t1) keep 77,386 and 64,786 rows and give the same orderings. An absorber passes the rule of §4.4: it built at least one own sigma, peaked at least one sigma from its normal level, and its absorption-side maker fills exceed its opposite fills to the peak; a median of 19 per event.
  • Population shock: with s=−d the absorption sign, dqi the MM’s position change over the run, sig24,i its own position scale and hitHYPE the run’s surge-side taker HYPE: Snet=∑i s·dqi / hitHYPE, the population’s net absorption as a share of the surge; Zmed=mediani(s·dqi / sig24,i), the typical MM’s shock in its own sigma; held(b)=∑i s·xi(b) / hitHYPE, the inventory still held at the end of bin b, from the position rebuild of §4.4, which covers the MMs whose accumulation reached half a sigma.
  • Lean at placement: dtouch is an order’s distance behind the same-side best quote at its own timestamp and dmid its distance from the mid, size-weighted per (event, MM, bin, side). tilttouch=dtouch(SAME)−dtouch(OPP), positive when the exit quote (OPP) is placed nearer the touch than the absorption quote (SAME); Δtilt=tilt(b)−tilt(PRE2H) against the same MM’s own two quiet hours before t0. The event’s value is the median over its MMs; “first 10 minutes” averages the bins [0, 5) and [5, 10).
  • Cancels and book pressure: excessexit=cancels per minute(OPP)−cancels per minute(SAME), a cancel counting in the bin of its cancel time; push=[cancelled size(OPP)+placed size(SAME)]−[cancelled size(SAME)+placed size(OPP)], in HYPE per bin, positive when the MM’s own book changes press the price the reversal way (on a buy surge: bids pulled, asks added).
  • Tests: Kruskal-Wallis across the five buckets and the Spearman with R(120) across events, oriented so that “the population presses the reversal” reads positive. Bonferroni thresholds: 0.001 for the 51 lean and cancel tests, 0.0008 for the 59 population tests.

One row is one measure averaged over the bins [0, 5) and [5, 10); a cell with five values is p5 / p25 / p50 / p75 / p95 across the bucket’s events of the event’s median over its D3d MMs, one value per line, median in bold. KW p is the Kruskal-Wallis p across the five buckets; the Spearman is against R(120) across the 922 events and is oriented so that “the population presses the reversal” reads positive, so every negative value here runs against that reading. With 51 tests the Bonferroni threshold is 0.001, which only the cancelled-order distance clears; that distance is U-shaped with the surge size (Q1 and Q5 highest) and carries no direction. The share row counts the 178,275 (event, MM, bin) rows of the two bins with push above and below zero; the rest, 20% to 22% of a bucket’s rows, are exactly zero. The 100-order floor and the absorber population give the same signs (tables/rvb0922_tests.csv). Source tables/rvb0922_tests.csv, rvb0922_place_event_bins.csv and rvb0922_place_mm_bins.parquet joined to rvb0922_pop_mm.csv, built by code/rvb0922_reduce.py.
  • MMs do not lean their quotes toward the exit more when the price reverts.
    In the first 10 minutes the lean against own PRE2H is +0.11 bps on Q1 and −0.17 on Q5 (Spearman −0.10 with R(120), rank test p = 0.010 against a 0.001 threshold), on quotes placed about 10 bps behind the touch, and the exit side takes half of the placed size in every bucket.
  • They do not cancel the reversal way either.
    The exit-side cancel excess and the book pressure have Spearman −0.11 and −0.12 with R(120), the wrong sign for pushing the price back; the gated-only and fixed-bps cuts give the same signs.
  • Every bucket leans toward the exit during the run and drops the lean at the run end
    , +0.36 to +0.65 bps in the last run bin and −0.07 to −0.20 in the first bin after it.
Figure 56. Cancels by side, by bucket

The chain from a bigger shock, through the lean, to a deeper reversal fails at both links. The first-10-minute lean has Spearman +0.04 with the population’s net absorption share and 0.00 with the typical MM’s own-sigma shock, and −0.10 with R(120). In a joint fit of R(120) on the post-run flow, the shock and the quoting measures, only the flow carries a coefficient distinguishable from zero, −40.8 bps per standard deviation. The book pressure does follow the population’s own absorption (Spearman +0.22) and goes with a shallower reversal, not a deeper one.

Table 69. The joint fit of the 120-minute return

Column key and source
The dependent variable is R(120) in bps. Each term is standardized over the estimation sample, so a coefficient is the change in R(120) for one standard deviation of the term. Standard errors are HC3. n = 921 (the spike-tick event is dropped for its peak move); R-squared 0.064, adjusted 0.056. The post-run imbalance is positive when the flow continues the surge, so its negative coefficient says flow against the surge deepens the reversal. Descriptive: the flow term shares its window with the outcome, and no coefficient identifies an effect. Source tables/rvb0922_ols.csv.

Remarks that need attention. Three readings that are not findings yet: each names what was seen, a possible design cause and the check.

  • After the run, the continuation bucket keeps a small lean toward the exit and the reversal buckets do not.
    Q1 holds +0.15 to +0.27 bps for the two hours, Q4 and Q5 sit at −0.01 to −0.17, and absorbers show the same ordering at three times the size (+0.78 against +0.16 in [5, 10)). Possible design cause: dtouch is read against the same-side best quote, and on a continuation the price keeps moving away from the exit side, so an MM that re-posts its exit quote at a fixed price behind a receding touch reads as leaning without having chosen to; on a reversal the exit touch comes toward the quote. Check: the same lean on dmid (Table 68, second row) orders the same way at −0.08, so the mid does not remove it; a check that would separate a decision from a receding touch is the lean on orders placed inside one second of a mid change, which the placement panel can supply.
  • The reversal buckets show more reversal-direction book pressure during the run and less after it.
    The last run bin has a median push of 14.9 HYPE on Q5 against 8.2 on Q1 (Figure 56), and the first 10 minutes after the run a p25 of −3.9 HYPE on Q5 against −0.6 on Q1. Possible design cause: push sums placed and cancelled size on both sides, and replace-quoting MMs cancel within a bin what they placed in it, so 20% to 22% of MM rows are exactly zero and the measure is carried by the MMs whose placements and cancels straddle a bin edge. Check: recompute push on net resting size at the bin’s last minute from the order state, which the minute-snapshot build already holds.
  • Q1 and Q5 are both big-surge ends.
    The peak move (medians 204 and 220 bps against 152 to 167 in Q2 to Q4) and the surge volume ($12.5m and $15.5m against $10.1m to $11.5m) are U-shaped across the buckets, so a raw bps return mixes surge size with direction; every HYPE-level sum in Table 66 inherits the U. Possible design cause: quintiles of a signed return put the largest moves of both signs in the end buckets. Check: G(120) buckets (the return over the peak move) and the gated-only cut in tables/rvb0922_event_returns.csv; the lean’s Spearman with G(120) is −0.12, the same sign and size as with R(120).
What this does not establish
  • R(120) and the post-run flow occupy the same window.
    The flow after the run and the price path it is compared against are contemporaneous, so the strongest separator restates the outcome in flow units as much as it explains it. Nothing here says the flow arrived before the price moved.
  • The quoting measures are small against the quoted distance.
    Every lean difference across buckets is under 0.3 bps at the event median on a placed distance of about 10 bps, and the MM-level interquartile range in a bin is about 7 bps. The section can say the population does not lean or cancel the reversal way; it cannot say the lean is zero.
  • The cancel and pressure measures are placement-and-cancel flows, not resting state.
    Replace-quoting puts a mass at exactly zero, and a bin edge decides whether a quote’s placement and cancel land in the same bin.
  • The absorber and shock counts stand on the D3d rule and the absorber rule of §4.4 as adopted.
    D3f (no fill gate) is under review; the floors of 50 and 100 in-window orders are reported beside D3d so the population choice can be revisited without a rerun.
  • No control windows carry the placement measures.
    The population-shock and flow measures could be benchmarked on the matched non-event windows; the placement panel was built for events only.

9.6 Shocked against unshocked MMs on F1

Set-up problem. The tables of this section come from the 2026-09-15 F1 build: an active MM there needs only a HYPE fill before and during the window (no post-only fill, no order floor; 118,269 F1 rows), and its order tables read the pre-fix order files, which drop 6.0% of F1 rows. §9.7 and Table 61 use newer populations. It should be rebuilt on the population of record (97,869 F1 rows) or retired in favor of §9.7.

F1 flags a shocked MM in 5.2% of active-MM rows, against 5.9% for the net-flow catalogue; §9.7 repeats this comparison on a newer build, against matched control windows.

Show the full section
  • ALO, IOC, GTC: order types: ALO is post-only (rejected if it would cross), IOC is immediate-or-cancel, GTC rests until cancelled.
  • Control window: for each event, the same clock time and length on the nearest day d + k (k = 1, −1, 2, …, −7) whose window, plus 2 hours on each side, overlaps no event of the same family (its 1-minute run or its box) and none of the 915 net-flow boxes; every 30-minute bin of it has taker flow, no data hole and a price, and it is not on 2025-10-10.
Terms used here: t0, t1 on a 30-minute box, HYPE MM, Active MM, SAME, OPP, Absorber, absorption rank, PRE2H, PRE30, POST, ALO, IOC, GTC, Submits, cancels, Censored, Quantile cells, Presence, Absorption share, 2025-10-10, v5d, Control window
  • t0, t1 on a 30-minute box: where a column measures an event on its 30-minute box (the F1 box, F2 box and net-flow columns), t0 and t1 are the open and the close of the box, in place of the run.
  • HYPE MM: a wallet the project's daily label model (v5d) classes as a HYPE market maker on that date. The label is per date.
  • Active MM: a labelled HYPE MM with at least one post-only (ALO) fill in the 2 hours before the event and at least one fill inside it. On a date whose whole population has no post-only fill in those 2 hours, a maker fill counts instead: 2026-04-16 to 2026-04-23, when the fill table has no time-in-force.
  • SAME, OPP: SAME is the MM side that absorbs the takers (asks when takers buy); OPP is the other side.
  • Absorber, absorption rank: an absorber is an active MM with maker fills on the absorption side during the event. Absorption rank orders them by that maker USD, 1 = largest.
  • PRE2H, PRE30, POST: PRE2H is the 2 hours ending at t0; PRE30 the last 30 minutes before t0; POST the 2 hours after t1.
  • ALO, IOC, GTC: order types: ALO is post-only (rejected if it would cross), IOC is immediate-or-cancel, GTC rests until cancelled.
  • Submits, cancels: new limit orders and cancels. The venue records a modify as one cancel plus one new order, so cancels per submit sits near 1.
  • Censored: the value hit the cap: the position had not come back by the end of the search window, so the true time is longer.
  • Quantile cells: a cell with five numbers is p5 / p25 / p50 / p75 / p95; with three, p25 / p50 / p75.
  • Presence: the share of the window's minutes in which the MM had at least one order resting on that side, counting minutes with no quote as zero.
  • Absorption share: an MM's maker USD on the absorption side of the event window, over all wallets' maker USD on that same side of that same window. It is at most 1, and the shares of the event's MMs sum to at most 1. Two statistics reuse the numerator with a different denominator: the concentration measures (effective N, top-5 share) divide by the total over the event's active MMs, so they describe concentration among MMs; the MM share of absorption keeps the denominator and sums the numerator over labelled MMs.
  • 2025-10-10: the liquidation-cascade day, kept in the row-level tables and named wherever it moves a result. On its 21:00 event 86.8% of absorbing-side maker USD ($517m of $596m) went to wallets with no MM label, against a median of 33.4% on other events, and 10 of 41 shocked MMs were shocked in the opposite direction.
  • v5d: the project's daily wallet label: a fixed set of threshold rules, not a fitted model, that reads each wallet's order records for one coin on one day and labels it market maker, frontend or algorithmic taker, in that order of test. It covers 2025-03-27 to 2026-06-30 and labels a wallet separately on each coin and date.
  • Control window: for each event, the same clock time and length on the nearest day d + k (k = 1, −1, 2, …, −7) whose window, plus 2 hours on each side, overlaps no event of the same family (its 1-minute run or its box) and none of the 915 net-flow boxes; every 30-minute bin of it has taker flow, no data hole and a price, and it is not on 2025-10-10. F3 uses the F1 controls of its own events. Controls are not matched on volume or volatility.

Cells as in Table 71. Absorption side is the maker side the event’s takers trade against, the side whose fills build the position (SAME); opposite side is the other (OPP). Rows down to traded volume are the variables of Table 9: counts, sizes, presence, submits, cancels and volume are averaged over every minute of the window with zero-quote minutes included; mean order size and the three distances are over minutes with at least one resting order on that side. Orders submitted: distinct order ids placed in the window (limit orders after the lifecycle filter of redef2_pop_orders.lifecycles: rejected, right-censored and TP/SL orders dropped). Orders live: distinct order ids resting at any point in the window. Fills: grouped_trade_oid rows of the wallet in the window; maker fills are the uncrossed ones; ALO fills have time_in_force Alo. For the net-flow catalogue orders submitted is recovered exactly as submits per minute times the window minutes and fills equal the builder’s trade count; orders live, maker fills and ALO fills were not stored in tables/redef2_pop_event_mm.csv (–). Source tables/review0915_fam_quantiles.csv, table = orders. Which rows this table uses. Every column of this table is over rows whose build date had a complete order read. redef2_pop_build.process_date reads order files for three placement days per build date, and on dates whose windows span more than that the days in between are never read, so every order placed on them is dropped as right-censored and the row carries zeros in all order-state columns. In the two pre-fix builds this table reads (tables/redef2_pop_event_mm.csv and the 2026-09-15 F1 run of code/review0915_fam_pop_build.py; the order-day-fixed rebuild behind §4 reads every placement day), that costs the net-flow table 32,489 of its 126,846 event rows (25.6%, its control windows widen the span) and the F1 run 7,087 of 118,269 (6.0%). Fills, positions and inventory are unaffected, so Table 71 uses all rows.

Column key and source
Variables of Table 32. PRE2H is the two hours before the window start; POST is the two hours after the window end, [t1, t1 + 2 h). F1 cells are p5 / p25 / p50 / p75 / p95 over window × MM rows; the median columns repeat the p50 for the other measurements. A median of levels is not a median of per-wallet changes, so a gap between the PRE2H and POST rows is indicative only. p, POST is the two-sided Mann-Whitney p-value of F1 shocked against F1 unshocked within POST. Source tables/review0915_fam_quantiles.csv, table = before_after, and tables/review0915_fam_pvalues.csv. The PRE2H rows repeat the prior-2-h rows of Table 72 by construction: the same columns over the same rows. All columns are over rows whose build date had a complete order read, as in Table 72.
  • F1 flags a shocked MM in 5.2% of active rows, against 5.9% for the net-flow catalogue.
    F1 has 6,173 shocked and 112,096 unshocked rows over 922 events, with a median 125 active MMs per event against 135. Its windows are a median 14 minutes against 30.
  • On the 30-minute boxes the same events flag 5.3% of rows.
    So the lower rate comes from which events the side-surge rule selects, not from its shorter windows.
  • Before the event, shocked MMs already hold a larger position relative to their own scale.
    Median |position| / own sig24, shocked against unshocked: F1 2.27 against 0.60; net-flow 2.93 against 0.59.
  • Shocked MMs trade more in the 30 minutes before.
    Median trades per bin, shocked against unshocked: F1 4.33 against 1.17; net-flow 3.33 against 1.00.
  • Shocked MMs rest more size on the absorption side than on the opposite side.
    In the prior 2 h the median is 362.6 against 273.3 HYPE in F1 (ratio 1.33) and 180.8 against 157.1 HYPE in net-flow (ratio 1.15).
  • The gap holds in the prior 30 min.
    F1 361.7 against 262.2 HYPE (ratio 1.38); net-flow 192.8 against 156.6 HYPE (ratio 1.23).
  • The half hours the net-flow rule never sees shock MMs at about half the rate of the overlapping half hours.
    In F1 the shocked share of rows is 6.0% over the 595 BOTH events against 3.7% over the 327 NEW_ONLY events; on the 30-minute boxes 6.2% against 3.5%. Roster shocks show the same gap in §9.3.
  • Shocked MMs absorb more of the event’s taker flow in both catalogues.
    The median shocked MM takes 0.8% of the event-side taker USD at rank 18 in F1, against 0.0% at rank 68 for the unshocked; net-flow 0.5% at rank 27 against 0.0% at rank 73.
  • Order and fill counts in the two hours before the event, median shocked against median unshocked: 3,533 against 628 orders submitted, 3,550 against 635 orders resting at some point, and 95 against 31 fills, of which 65 against 21 are ALO (post-only) fills. Submitted and live are within 1% of each other: almost every order a wallet has resting in the window was also placed inside it.
  • The order tables drop rows with an incomplete order read.
    In the pre-fix builds these are 32,489 of the net-flow table’s 126,846 event rows (25.6%) and 7,087 of F1’s 118,269 (6.0%); §4 uses the order-day-fixed rebuild, which has none. The state table keeps them, since fills and positions are unaffected.

9.7 The population statistics and the absorber pass on F1, F3 and F2, against matched controls

Set-up problem. Every table of this section is on the earlier active-MM rule (post-only fill in PRE2H, no order floor): 112,425 F1 event rows and 922 F1 control windows. The population of record has 97,869 F1 rows and 920 F1 control windows, but the F2 events have no rebuild on it, so the section was not moved. It should be rebuilt on the population of record for all six event sets.

Every event set shocks four to seven times as many MMs as the same clock time on a quiet day, and in every set the five largest absorbers take about 30% of the surging side’s taker USD while the end rule flags 18% to 28% of them.

Show the full section
  • End rule, peak rule: the end rule flags |position at t1 − position at t0| ≥ 3 sig24; the peak rule applies the same test to the largest gap from the t0 position at any minute inside the window.
  • Absorber, absorption rank: an absorber is an active MM with maker fills on the absorption side during the event.
  • PRE2H, PRE30, POST: PRE2H is the 2 hours ending at t0; PRE30 the last 30 minutes before t0; POST the 2 hours after t1.
Terms used here: t0, t1 on a 30-minute box, Active MM, End rule, peak rule, Absorber, absorption rank, PRE2H, PRE30, POST, ALO, IOC, GTC, Censored, Quantile cells, Absorption share, 2025-10-10, Event classes, Control window
  • t0, t1 on a 30-minute box: where a column measures an event on its 30-minute box (the F1 box, F2 box and net-flow columns), t0 and t1 are the open and the close of the box, in place of the run.
  • Active MM: a labelled HYPE MM with at least one post-only (ALO) fill in the 2 hours before the event and at least one fill inside it. On a date whose whole population has no post-only fill in those 2 hours, a maker fill counts instead: 2026-04-16 to 2026-04-23, when the fill table has no time-in-force.
  • End rule, peak rule: the end rule flags |position at t1 − position at t0| ≥ 3 sig24; the peak rule applies the same test to the largest gap from the t0 position at any minute inside the window.
  • Absorber, absorption rank: an absorber is an active MM with maker fills on the absorption side during the event. Absorption rank orders them by that maker USD, 1 = largest.
  • PRE2H, PRE30, POST: PRE2H is the 2 hours ending at t0; PRE30 the last 30 minutes before t0; POST the 2 hours after t1.
  • ALO, IOC, GTC: order types: ALO is post-only (rejected if it would cross), IOC is immediate-or-cancel, GTC rests until cancelled.
  • Censored: the value hit the cap: the position had not come back by the end of the search window, so the true time is longer.
  • Quantile cells: a cell with five numbers is p5 / p25 / p50 / p75 / p95; with three, p25 / p50 / p75.
  • Absorption share: an MM's maker USD on the absorption side of the event window, over all wallets' maker USD on that same side of that same window. It is at most 1, and the shares of the event's MMs sum to at most 1. Two statistics reuse the numerator with a different denominator: the concentration measures (effective N, top-5 share) divide by the total over the event's active MMs, so they describe concentration among MMs; the MM share of absorption keeps the denominator and sums the numerator over labelled MMs.
  • 2025-10-10: the liquidation-cascade day, kept in the row-level tables and named wherever it moves a result. On its 21:00 event 86.8% of absorbing-side maker USD ($517m of $596m) went to wallets with no MM label, against a median of 33.4% on other events, and 10 of 41 shocked MMs were shocked in the opposite direction.
  • Event classes: liquidation cascade: forced flow at least 10% of taker USD; otherwise big price move: the mid moved at least 168 bps from start to end, the top 5% of all half hours; otherwise no big price move.
  • Control window: for each event, the same clock time and length on the nearest day d + k (k = 1, −1, 2, …, −7) whose window, plus 2 hours on each side, overlaps no event of the same family (its 1-minute run or its box) and none of the 915 net-flow boxes; every 30-minute bin of it has taker flow, no data hole and a price, and it is not on 2025-10-10. F3 uses the F1 controls of its own events. Controls are not matched on volume or volatility.

Event sets: F1 (922 one-sided events), F3 (its 327 side-only events), F2 (399 two-sided events), each on its 1-minute run, with F2 also on its 30-minute boxes; the net-flow catalogue (915 events, 30-minute boxes) is the section 4 population of record: all 915 events on the order-day-fixed build, under the same active-MM rule. Every table includes every date, 2025-10-10 and 2026-01-31 among them, and uses the active-MM rule and the complete order read of section 4. The 1-minute run is the window of record for the families, and the two-sided run is measured on excess total taker USD.

Symbols used in this section
  • F1 also net-flow: the other 595 F1 events, whose box does overlap a net-flow event. F1 = these 595 plus the 327 of F3, so the two columns split F1 and neither is a new build.
  • F2 run: F2’s 1-minute run is built on excess total taker USD, Xt = (Bt + St) − the median of B + S over the previous 6 hours, entered at 3 times and left below 0.25 times its 6-hour 95th percentile; its direction is the sign of the run’s cumulative net taker flow.
  • dq: position at t1 minus position at t0, in HYPE.
  • Absorbing direction: the position moved the way a maker filling the surging takers moves (shorter into taker buying, longer into taker selling). For F2 and for controls, the side is the one the event’s net flow points to.
  • End rule against peak rule, an example
    : an MM with sig24 = 2,000 HYPE that is 7,000 HYPE longer ten minutes in and 4,000 HYPE longer at t1 is flagged by the peak rule (7,000 ≥ 6,000) and not by the end rule (4,000 < 6,000).
  • Top-5 absorbers: absorption ranks 1 to 5 of the window’s active MMs.
  • What the shocked MMs earn on the fills is set by the price move, not by which rule selected the event.
    Median maker M30 of shocked rows: -22.1 bps on the big-price-move events of F1 also net-flow and -19.9 bps on those of the net-flow catalogue, against +3.2 bps and -1.5 bps where the box has no big move. F3 and F2 hold few big moves, so their pooled medians are near zero (+1.9 and -0.5 bps) while F1 as a whole is -6.2 bps.
  • The five largest absorbers carry the same third of the flow in every family, and the same minority of them is flagged.
    Median combined share of the surging side’s taker USD: F1 30.1%; F1 also net-flow 29.5%; F3 31.1%; F2 30.0%; net-flow 29.8%. Share of their rows the end rule flags: F1 24.5%; F1 also net-flow 28.2%; F3 17.8%; F2 18.3%; net-flow 23.7%. No top-5 absorber is flagged in 36.3% of F1 events and 39.0% of net-flow events.
  • They escape the rule by their own scale in every family, as in section 8.
    The unshocked top-5 absorbers sit at the 94th to 95th percentile of own sig24 among the event’s active MMs and the 97th of HYPE peak excursion, and their peak excursion in own sig24 has median 1.7 (F1), 1.9 (F1 also net-flow), 1.5 (F3), 2.4 (F2), 2.1 (net-flow), all below the threshold of 3. The share that never reaches 3 sig24 at any minute of the window is F1 84.0%; F1 also net-flow 82.0%; F3 87.4%; F2 65.0%; net-flow 73.9%.
  • In a two-sided event the inventory comes back inside the window, so the peak rule adds much more than it does elsewhere.
    Top-5 absorber rows flagged, end rule against peak rule: F1 24.5% against 36.6%, F2 18.3% against 46.9%. It is not only that F2 windows are longer: at a matched 11 to 20 minutes the peak rule flags 36.8% of F1 top-5 rows against 24.5% under the end rule (1.5×), and 34.9% against 14.6% in F2 (2.4×); the median share of the peak still held at t1 is 0.91 in F1 and 0.66 in F2.
  • The small resting book of the F2 shocked MMs is a different mix of wallets, not the same wallets quoting less.
    Median absorption-side resting size in PRE2H is 388 HYPE for F1 shocked rows and 65 HYPE for F2, but on the 388 of the 426 wallets shocked in both that rest size on both sides, the per-wallet ratio of the two medians is 0.90 (p25 0.51, p75 1.14).

Remarks that need attention.

  • F3’s big-price-move events cost the shocked MMs almost nothing: -1.4 bps against -22.1 bps in F1 also net-flow,
    although the class rule is the same and the median move is close (177 against 205 bps). Test that would settle it: pair F3 and F1 also net-flow big-move events on |price move| and on hit-side taker USD, and compare the shocked rows’ M30 within the pairs; if the gap survives, split the markout by whether the MM was on the side the price ran into.
  • The control windows are not empty: 1.4% of net-flow control rows and 0.9% of F1 control rows clear |dq| ≥ 3 × sig24,
    and 34.9% of F1 control windows hold at least one such row. Test: measure how much of that is inventory carried into the control window from a nearby event (the exclusion is 2 hours) by recomputing the control shocked share against the distance to the nearest event of any catalogue.
  • Seven F1 rows (and seven F2 rows) are marked as having complete order state yet carry no resting order at all in PRE2H while the wallet has post-only fills in that window.
    Test: for those wallet-dates, check whether the order file holds the order ids behind those fills; if it does not, the coverage rule (half the maker-fill order ids found) is passing a wallet whose orders are missing for another reason.
Every event set against its matched controls
  • Every event set shocks four to seven times as many MMs as the same clock time on a quiet day.
    Shocked share of active-MM rows, event against its matched control: F1 5.3% against 0.9% (6.1×); F1 also net-flow 6.1% against 0.9% (6.6×); F3 3.8% against 0.8% (4.8×); F2 6.2% against 1.3% (4.7×); net-flow 6.0% against 1.4% (4.3×). Per pair, the event’s shocked share is the higher one in 84.6% of the 922 F1 pairs and 85.5% of the 399 F2 pairs.
  • In an event the shocked MMs move the way a maker filling the surging takers moves; in a control they do not.
    Share of shocked rows in the absorbing direction, event against control: F1 90.2% against 47.7%; F1 also net-flow 91.6% against 48.0%; F3 85.5% against 47.2%; F2 68.9% against 41.5%; net-flow 87.0% against 47.5%. The two-sided family is the exception that follows from its definition: its two sides are balanced, so the run’s net direction carries little information, and on the 30-minute box it falls to 51.0%, which is chance.
  • The half hours only the one-sided rule sees shock MMs at two thirds the rate of the half hours both rules see.
    F3 (side-only) 3.8% of rows against 6.1% for the F1 events the net-flow rule also flags; their controls are 0.8% and 0.9%, so the gap is in the events, not in the baseline. F3 windows are shorter (12 minutes against 16) and their price moves smaller (109 bps against 156 bps at the median).
Set-up problem. This table is still on the earlier active-MM rule: F1 112,425 event rows and 922 control windows, net-flow 120,269 event rows. On the population of record the F1 column has 97,869 rows and 920 controls and the net-flow column 101,245 rows, and F1 shocks 5.9% of rows against 1.0% in its controls (6.2×), against 5.3% and 0.9% (6.1×) here; the F2 columns have no rebuild. It should be rebuilt on the population of record for all six columns.

Column key and source
Columns are event sets. Events rows are over event windows; controls rows over their matched control windows (no controls are built for the F2 30-minute boxes). Shocked: |dq| ≥ 3 × sig24 over the window (end rule). Absorbing direction: share of shocked rows whose position moved the way a maker filling the surging takers moves; in a control window the side is borrowed from the matched event, so 50% is the no-information value. Shocked share per window is n shocked / n active in one window, p5 / p25 / p50 / p75 / p95 over windows. Event minus control is that share in the event less the share in its own control, over event-control pairs. Active MMs, sig24, dq: see the symbols list. Sources tables/review0917_fam_summary.csv, tables/review0917_fam_pairs.csv, from code/review0917_fam_reduce.py over data/redef2_pop_parts_all_{F1of,F2,F2box,famctrl}act (built 2026-09-17 by code/review0917_fam_pop_build.py) and data/redef2_pop_parts_all_orderfixact for the net-flow column. The shocked share of all rows is the share the median per-window share does not show: large windows carry more rows. Population: active MMs with a HYPE fill in PRE2H and in the window and a post-only fill in PRE2H, without the order floor of the population of record; the population of record is rebuilt for F1, its controls and the net-flow boxes but not for the F2 events, so the table stays on one rule.

Column key and source
Rows are one variable per event set. Cells are p5 / p25 / p50 / p75 / p95 over window × active MM rows, one quantile per line. Shocked and unshocked are event rows split by the end rule (|dq| ≥ 3 × sig24); control is every active MM row of the matched control windows. PRE2H is the 2 hours before the window start t0, PRE30 the 30 minutes before it; a bin is 5 minutes. |position| / own sig24 divides the absolute HYPE position at t0 by the MM’s 24-hour robust inventory scale. Absorption share is the MM’s maker USD on the absorption side over all surging-side taker USD in the window; rank orders the window’s active MMs by that USD (1 = largest). Maker M30 is the 30-minute markout of the MM’s maker fills in the window, basis points (bps) of volume. Source tables/review0917_fam_quantiles.csv, table = state.

Column key and source
Cells as in the state table: p5 / p25 / p50 / p75 / p95 over window × active MM rows. Absorption side is the maker side the surging takers trade against; opposite side the other. Resting size is HYPE resting on that side, averaged over every minute of the window, zero-quote minutes included. Best-level distance is the distance of the closest resting order from the mid in basis points (bps), over minutes with an order on that side. Orders submitted: distinct limit order ids placed in PRE2H (rejected, right-censored and TP/SL orders dropped). Post-only fills: fills on time-in-force ALO orders. Rows: only those whose order state is complete, i.e. every placement-day file from the day before t0 − 2 h to the day of t1 + 2 h exists and at least half the order ids behind the MM’s own maker fills in [t0 − 2 h, t1 + 2 h) are in the order store. Source tables/review0917_fam_quantiles.csv, table = orders.

Column key and source
Columns are event sets. Top-5 absorbers are absorption ranks 1 to 5 (maker USD on the absorption side in the window). Share of hit-side taker USD: their combined maker USD on the absorption side over all surging-side taker USD, per event. Share of MM absorption: the same USD over all active MMs’ absorption-side maker USD, per event. sig24 percentile: rank of the MM’s own 24-hour inventory scale among the event’s active MMs (100% = largest). Peak excursion: max over the window’s minutes of |q(t) − q(t0)|, as a percentile among the event’s active MMs, and divided by sig24. Quantile cells are p5 / p25 / p50 / p75 / p95 over events (shares) or over event × MM rows (the rest). End and peak rules as in the previous table. Source tables/review0917_fam_absorbers.csv.

Table 79. The three family catalogues.

familyfileeventsdefinition
F1tables/redef4_events_F1_one_sided.csv922one-sided side-surge events at the matched count, BOTH plus NEW_ONLY
F2tables/redef4_events_F2_two_sided.csv399two-sided events at the same cutoffs with |buys − sells| / (buys + sells) under 1/3 at the peak bin

Column key and source
Each file carries the 132 columns of tables/redef_imb_events_recommended_1m.csv in order and with the same meanings, then 51 new columns covering the set, the family, the 5-minute duration run, the five 1-minute anchors, the price statistics and the three gates. start_utc is t0, end_excl_utc is t1 (end_utc is the open of the last run minute, t1−1 min) and peak_utc is tc; the §3 convention of the largest in-direction minute remains available as peak_utc_1m. Source tables/redef4_validation.csv.
  • The MM outcome pass is run on all three families.
    F1 against the net-flow catalogue in §9.6; F1, F3 and F2, each against quiet windows at the same clock time, in §9.7.
  • The two-sided family needs one construction choice.
    Total taker USD is positive and right-skewed, so an exit threshold at a quarter of its 6-hour p95 sits near the median of the baseline and a run on it would cover half of every window. The run measure used is the excess over the 6-hour median total, which puts a median 23% of baseline minutes above the exit threshold, close to the 20% the one-sided net measure gives.
